svg.title: Async-RBench: key evaluation mechanisms
svg.desc: Task-grounded paired evaluation. Shared participant-safe task inputs and matched benchmark-owned initial workstreams enter independent Linear and Async routes. The private event contract covers eight benchmark event themes and defines affected and preserved work without revealing scoring truth to the model. Linear runs concurrent initial children and waits for all terminal states before one stable atomic bundle reaches the main model. Async permits ongoing main work, policy-gated result release and queued actual model presentation with bounded response windows. The main model chooses selective revision and preservation. Controlled delivery groups the kernel gateway and fixed-adapter main-agent input; these have distinct ownership. Queued results count as presented only when included in an actual model request. Public submission checks determine acceptance; hidden semantic checks do not suppress deliveries. The evaluator execution trace records delivery, actual presentation, agent actions and event-boundary artifact digests as scoring evidence. Linear BTS and Async BTS evaluate their final states independently. Async DRS uses evaluator event/state evidence and private event-outcome checks, half process plus half outcome per event. No claim is made that current DRS is strictly bounded by a single presentation window. Each metric aggregates repeats and tasks before an equal-weight mean across event themes, with coverage reported separately; this is not a direct average of individual DRS events.
